verdict.rationale: Cursor Automations let users define triggers that run cloud agents automatically. Triggers can be events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks or Linear (PR opened, pushed or merged, comments, labels), or cron schedules. Users can describe the rule in plain language via the /automate skill, and agent-loop hooks add event-driven rules locally. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of event-triggered automations working as documented.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Cursor Automations run cloud agents in the background, either on a schedule or in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear, and more.
The `/automate` skill lets you describe the workflow you want in plain language. Cursor configures the automation's triggers, instructions, and tools for you.
Hooks let you observe, control, and extend the agent loop using custom scripts
